subject: [enc4k] restart-on-switch done (vcodecd+probe, IP 1091/1091, payload-vcodec-rs); 0312 kern.n2vc.venc_fast patch + build_q10jg.sh recipe (not built)
body: (B) vc18 failure = HEVC SEQ_HDR IPI timed out (-60) after two H.264 sessions, then the daemon requested a guest stop: E_GUEST detail 7 = n2a32 stop reason REQUEST (vpud+0x27c0). Not reproducible with the host fake. Fix: vcodecd --restart-on-switch: an OPEN of another codec than the previous session's -> ERROR BUSY detail N2VCD_DETAIL_RESTART (0x52535452, include/n2vcd_proto.h), VENC powered off, exit 75; launchd KeepAlive restarts (start->serving 0.26 s on the phone). Same codec reopens stay in-process. Probe: on BUSY/RESTART, E_GUEST or a lost server under OPEN it re-execs the same session (no gate/delay, --wait-server 30), max 2. stage-vcodec.sh --keepalive adds --restart-on-switch (plan restart_on_switch) only if the staged vcodecd knows it; guest-vcodec.sh appends it. Tests: t_daemon scenario_restart_on_switch; host e2e ladder with a launchd-like loop: 5/5 sessions, two restarts. payload-vcodec-rs = vcodecd 6cb118ae (current tree) + probe 073cd6cd + --keepalive, ladder H.264 High / HEVC Main: PAYLOAD=payload-vcodec-rs ... txn.sh $IMG vc22-rs. (C) kern/p031x/0312-nord2-vcodec-venc-fast.patch (on 0310; also applies to the live kern/bsd/dev source): SYSCTL kern.n2vc.venc_fast 0/1 (EINVAL otherwise, logs 'NORD2 VCODEC: kern.n2vc.venc_fast a -> b'); RWVC_POWER passes 624 MHz when 1; n2vc_hw_on still muxes only with VEN+VENC_C1 off. The library power-cycles VENC around every frame, so a write applies at the next frame. Compiled: q10at3 stage + 0298 + 0310 + 0312, sweet_touch.c with -Wall -Wextra -Werror OK. Recipe gpu/build/build_q10jg.sh = q10jf + 0312 (NOT built). Phone use: sysctl -w kern.n2vc.venc_fast=1 before the probe (or add to the probe later). Vcore: our kernel never writes DVFSRC/VCORE (only reads: 0121 n2dram DVFSRC dump, 0284 VCORE PMIC snapshot); Linux raises vcore to OPP1 for venc_step0 (mmdvfs). JPEG already ran at 624 MHz. Cheapest safe step: boot once with n2dram=1 to log the DVFSRC level before trusting long 624 MHz encodes; no DVFSRC write proposed. Core 1: the logs show VENC core 0 and core 1 powered alternately per frame, never overlapping (vendor ping-pong, serialised by our synchronous encode): no parallelism. 4K 68.8 vs 1080p 29.3 ms => ~16 ms fixed per-frame overhead + ~13 ms HW per 1080p-equivalent; at 624 MHz 4K is ~39 ms (~25 fps) unless the per-frame power cycle/IPI overhead is cut (keep VENC powered during a session) or two frames are pipelined on the two cores.
